originality.rationale: The precise claim is the six-sector Gram spectrum, parity reversal of sharp Riesz extremizers, and universal sharp condition-number maximum, not the degree-two rank. Bernasconi-Egidi and Venkitesh already determine Hilbert-function ranks, and Filmus provides harmonic Johnson eigenspaces. The new Gram weight is the uniform distribution on a disconnected residue-class union of Hamming shells. Root-of-unity moments and coupling of constant and edge sectors yield a new quantitative spectrum; none of the inspected full-source portions states its particular eigenvalue list or universal extremal value. Bounded novelty review cannot exclude an equivalent historic spectral formulation.
residual_risks: The original 1999 Bernasconi–Egidi full text was unavailable; its Hilbert theorem covers rank, and any additional unreviewed quantitative formula could affect spectral novelty.
Published Hamming-shell research record files were not available for full-text inspection; their available scientific summaries concern a single fixed-weight layer.
Other association-scheme or coding-theory spectral treatments could express the same modular-three Gram theorem under different notation.

value.rationale: The natural nonzero ternary single-parity-check ensemble is a nontrivial disconnected union of Boolean shells. Exact inversion stability for all quadratic Walsh coefficients is not determined by older rank results. The theorem identifies every mode, a sharp first recovery dimension, parity-dependent least stable modes, an exact universal conditioning optimum and exponentially rapid asymptotic tightness. These properties are structural and cover all n≥8, rather than an arbitrary small numerical census.
